source.title: Forgetting Only What Matters: Layer-Selective Unlearning toward Robust LLMs
source.authors: Ravi Ranjan; Olivera Kotevska; Agoritsa Polyzou

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or text corruption; full paper and appendices are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests post-unlearning quantization and prompt attacks, and reports both remaining recovery and a method intended to resist it. Its results refine the claim: recovery increases under these conditions, but the reported scores remain low and FOM-UL fares better than the compared methods.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own layer-ablation procedure as a diagnostic for layer localization, but gives no result showing that ablating an activation direction restores forgotten knowledge. It does not test recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated or small relearning sets. Table 6's bin-crossing and update-ratio results are mechanism measurements, not direct measures of recovered behavior. Results cited from other work are not included.
record.test_reason: The paper measures, on Llama-3.2-1B/TOFU, whether forgotten content returns after 8-bit/4-bit post-training quantization (D) and under paraphrase, alternate-template and jailbreak prompts (E). It covers six baseline unlearning methods and its own FOM-UL, which it presents as a robust counter-method (F). It uses ROUGE-based M1/M2 rather than the originals' accuracy measures, so this is a different method aimed at the same question.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude FOM-UL reduces residual memorization with utility near vanilla and is more robust than baselines to jailbreak prompts and 8/4-bit quantization, without formal erasure guarantees. They also state that clean-prompt metrics understate residual knowledge, since recovery rises for all methods under prompt shifts.
record.recipe_differences: FOM-UL selects layers using forget-to-retain gradient scores and applies masked updates with forget, mismatch, and retain losses; it is not a reproduction of the listed original unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Quantization precision (FP32, 8-bit, 4-bit), prompt format (clean, paraphrased, alternate QA, jailbreak), and selected layer budget/location affect reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Table 6 bin-crossing analysis under 4-bit: FOM-UL 5.6% of updated weights cross a quantization bin vs 0.7–2.8% for baselines (ρ ratio 1.18 vs 0.31–0.74).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Quantization recovery arises because diffuse unlearning updates stay within quantization bins; concentrated layer updates survive rounding more often.

record.problems: The directly relevant attack and quantization tables do not report uncertainty. The paper does not provide a never-trained or chance-level comparison for recovery scores. The versions of the prompt attacks are limited to the described QA templates and jailbreak wrappers.
record.rows_left_out: Kept the main memorization measures and attack leakage results for the quantization and prompt settings, plus a clean utility check. Omitted M1adv and M3adv from Table 8, other clean-evaluation values in Tables 1–2, and layer-budget sensitivity results in Table 9; these are either additional metrics for the same attack findings or not direct recovery measures. Table 6 bin-crossing measurements are mentioned in gate_note because they do not measure recovered behavior.

untested.parts: Near-chance targeted accuracy: no retrained-model or chance reference is given for M1/M2. The attack-robustness part is recorded under D/E (baselines) and F (FOM-UL).
Entirely untested; no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
Entirely untested. Layer ablation is used only to choose layers, not to recover forgotten knowledge.
Only bitsandbytes 8-bit and 4-bit, only Llama-3.2-1B on TOFU; no other quantizers, models or datasets.
Other languages and in-context information are untested. Paraphrase and alternate-template results are reported only for FOM-UL, not for the baselines.
FOM-UL is not tested against fine-tuning/relearning or internal-edit attacks.

missing.what: Qualitative int4 recovery example: GA-unlearned model reproduces the forgotten answer after int4; NPO-style recovers partially; FOM-UL stays stable.
Retain utility M4 under quantization falls for all methods (e.g., GAGDR 2.07→1.67 at 4-bit; FOM-UL 2.90→2.04).
M1adv values under jailbreaks for all methods (e.g., GAGDR 5.05, FOM-UL 1.78). The record declares these as left out.

record.verdict_notes: The paper proposes its own method, so its F evidence is self-reported. Several internal inconsistencies should lower confidence. Section 5 claims 1.22% residual memorization at 4-bit, but Table 3 gives 2.44. Table 2's BOOKS columns duplicate NEWS. Tables 3, 8 and 10 report no std despite 'three runs' elsewhere. The reproducibility section describes a Harry Potter forget set while the main results use TOFU. Table 11 uses a fictional 'Crimson Harbor' prompt labelled BOOKS-style. No verdict is given for A: the near-chance part is not measurable here, and the attack-robustness part is recorded under D/E for baselines and F for FOM-UL. Recovery fractions are computed against vanilla M1/M2 of 5.80 from Table 1.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report targeted-knowledge accuracy against chance or a never-trained model as the reference; reports ROUGE-style memorization scores instead.
Recovery from unrelated, loosely related, or partial-fact fine-tuning is not evaluated.
No post-unlearning activation-direction ablation or evidence that a tested method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Tests post-training 8-bit and 4-bit quantization, not every quantization method or bit width.
Tests paraphrased prompts, alternate QA templates, and jailbreak wrappers; other languages and in-context information are not tested.
FOM-UL is tested against quantization and prompt attacks, but not against the fine-tuning or internal-edit attacks named in the claim.

source_check.notes: M1 equals M2 in nearly every Llama-3.2-1B cell (Tables 1, 3, 8), so the two are not independent measures. Table 3 has no std and no quantized-vanilla reference, so gaps use FP32 vanilla 5.80. Section 5's 1.22% at 4-bit contradicts Table 3 (2.44). The F results test the authors' own method and have not been replicated independently.

statements.correction: 2609.10439, Llama-3.2-1B, TOFU-World Facts, bitsandbytes: all 7 methods rise at both 8-bit and 4-bit. Full recovery at 4-bit (>= vanilla 5.80): GAGDR 4.24->5.94, ReLearn 5.04->5.80. Partial at 4-bit: NPOGDR 2.06->3.68, KLDGDR 4.04->4.32, SURE+NPO 1.60->2.42, LUNAR 1.28->3.88, FOM-UL 1.24->2.44. At 8-bit, rises cover about 8-76% of the gap. Table 3 has no std; Table 1 is mean±std over three runs.
statements.problem: Numbers are right, but 'In each study, other settings show no recovery' is wrong here: every other Table 3 cell rises partly. Table 3 also gives no std.

statements.correction: 8-bit M1: KLDGDR 4.04 to 4.18 (about 8% of gap), ReLearn 5.04 to 5.62 (about 76%).

This study (Llama-3.2-1B, TOFU-World Facts, bitsandbytes): LUNAR M1/M2 1.28 at FP32 -> 3.14 at 8-bit and 3.88 at 4-bit, about 41% and 58% of the gap to vanilla 5.80. That is partial recovery (D limits_scope), not a no-change or fall result.
statements.problem: Cites q4-lunar-m1 as evidence that LUNAR barely moves under quantization (label challenges). In this study LUNAR shows one of the largest rises.

Listing 2609.10439 (TOFU, Llama-3.2-1B) as reproducing 4-bit recovery is right: GAGDR 5.94 and ReLearn 5.80 reach vanilla 5.80, and all other methods rise partly.
Jailbreak M2adv recovers 13-74% of the gap to vanilla 5.80 (FOM-UL 13%, ReLearn 74%); NPOGDR 2.06 to 3.16.

This study: FOM-UL (the authors' own method), Llama-3.2-1B, TOFU-World Facts. M2 is 1.24 clean, 1.58 paraphrase, 1.66 alternate templates and 1.84 jailbreak (average of four wrappers). ALR goes 8.7 -> 10.3, 10.9, 11.6. Lowest jailbreak M2adv and ALR among 8 methods. Reviewed (AACL-IJCNLP 2026), code.

statements.problem: Cites the FOM-UL quantization rows under a 'challenges' claim about MUSE without naming the study. The rows are TOFU-World Facts and show partial resistance, not absent resistance (verdict l4 limits_scope).
